note: THE WORKFLOW TABLE. SPEC-terrain §15.1 makes this artifact authoritative over SEQUENCING — the states, their order, which of them wait for the owner, which write which artifact, and which reach a judgment point — from the moment it exists and not before. It is authoritative over NOTHING ELSE: every semantic contract in §§2-14 (what a claim says, which members are placed, whether a figure is honest, what the grammar admits) is untouched by this file and is not readable from it. The executor is a generic interpreter of this table and holds no state list of its own.
licensed_by: v1, kogaki#625, owner selection 2026-08-23 at the /ship-cycle 625 sitting, executing SPEC-terrain §15 (Status v23). Mints the table as a carrier and declares the baseline states. THE BASELINE CORRECTS THE ISSUE'S OWN: kogaki#625 named the table as `survey -> TAG-SELECTION (wait) -> screen render -> ID-SELECTION (wait) -> full report -> done`, which omits compose-input and its composition pin, the two judgment points as states, the tag-screen state, and TWO of the four owner waits — the terrain-trim-ratification gate and the terrain-strand-selection gate the flow actually ends at (.claude/skills/terrain/SKILL.md steps 5-6, 'The flow ends at step 6'). Acceptance item 2 counts waits and writes against this table, so a table declaring two waits would have passed its own check while dropping shipped contract. Recorded here rather than only in the issue because this file is what a later reader counts against. | v2, kogaki#625, PR #626 round 1 (2026-08-23): three reviewer findings, all against v1's own encoding rather than its content. Prose members `rule` and `why_they_survive` moved out of the name-keyed maps into sibling `_note` fields — an interpreter enumerating those objects read them as two phantom entry points, in a file whose own note calls its conformance mechanically checkable. `renders_gate_declaration` declared explicitly on every state rather than carried by absence. `done` re-typed to a new `terminal` kind, because `compute` — "does not stop" — gave a generic executor no way to read the end of the run from the table.

encoding_choice.chosen: An ordered state array in JSON, each state declaring its kind, its writes, its judgment point and its wait binding.
encoding_choice.declined: A state-transition graph with explicit edges. The flow is a line with one conditional state; edges would encode a generality nothing in §15.4 asks for, and an unreachable edge is a defect a linear array cannot express.
encoding_choice.recorded_here_because: SPEC §15.1 names this file and its duties and deliberately does not decide its encoding, exactly as §14.1 leaves report-format.json's encoding to the artifact.

ratification.procedure: An issue licenses the change; a dated owner decision settles whatever in it is a decision rather than a transcription; the edit lands here; the version integer is bumped and a licensed_by clause is appended.
ratification.this_file_carries_a_pointer_never_a_verd: Where an entry records an owner ruling, the ruling's home is the issue named beside it.
ratification.not_enforced: Nothing denies an edit here that no issue licensed. The version and licensed_by fields are a ledger for readers and gate no code path — declared at SPEC §15.8 rather than left to be discovered.

state_kinds.compute: Runs, writes no owner artifact, does not stop.
state_kinds.write: Runs a renderer bound to it and writes exactly one owner artifact. The renderer is private to the executor (SPEC §15.5).
state_kinds.judgment: Reaches a declared judgment point. The judgment arrives as a typed record; the executor validates and never composes it (SPEC §15.6).
state_kinds.wait: The executor stops. Nothing further runs until the owner speaks and the session re-enters (SPEC §15.2, §15.4).
state_kinds.terminal: The run is over. Runs nothing, writes nothing, and the executor stops without awaiting an owner. Distinct from `compute` because a generic interpreter holds no state list of its own (SPEC §15.1) and must read the end from the table rather than from position (PR #626 round 1, finding 4).

screen.writer: one private screen renderer, called by every state whose writes field names it
screen.rule: overwritten on every render; ONE writer (SPEC §15.5, superseding §14.4.1's two-writer class)

full_report.rule: overwritten per pull; identity is §12.1's triple

states.does: Reads the seam once (element_survey), composes Lesson candidates and Journey marks, mints every display_id, validates, writes the survey record to the run workspace.
states.note: The survey record IS the ID->slug map (§14.3). The run record references it by path and copies nothing out of it (§15.3).

states.does: Renders the tag screen the owner chooses from.
states.note: Formerly the standalone `view` subcommand, whose direct unguarded write to reports/Screen.md is the defect §15.5 names. As a state its render goes through the one screen writer and therefore through the format guard.
The owner SPEAKING, not the runtime asking. No prompt, no selector, no question UI — §6.3's allowlist for the window this wait opens is empty.

states.does: Bounded tag-scoped read; emits the composition pin naming the tag, the survey pin and the member set served per group.
states.note: Composes nothing and judges nothing. Its pin is what makes composing outside the bounded read unproducible.

states.input_shape: typed claims record carrying composition_pin and one claim per group
states.refusal: claims whose group/member set is not a subset of the composition pin are refused, naming the members outside it

states.input_shape: typed per-group record, judged: true, one entry per composed group, carrying the judge pin
states.refusal: a missing group entry, a bare array, or an absent judge pin is refused; the leaf condition is evaluated from the supplied verdicts and never invented

states.does: Renders the co-tag screen: groups by co-tag, mints GroupIDs, renders the composed claims and the SubGroups J2 placed.

states.note: The owner SPEAKING. The ids are valid for the run that printed them; a pin advance may renumber, and the run record is what makes 'this run' nameable.

states.does: One Full Report over exactly the entered set, idempotent per §12.1's identity triple, carrying the provenance-neighborhood section.

states.conditional: entered only when a trim is proposed
states.owner_supplies: ratification of the trim, or its negation
states.note: A declared gate, and always was. The record carries the machine premise and its negation as a first-class option; never trim silently.

states.owner_supplies: up to three Strand ids, or free text
states.note: The declaration is rendered through AskUserQuestion exactly as declared — options verbatim, nothing pre-selected, free text always on — and the answer is captured with its tool_use_id. More than three ids is a trim and is refused.

states.does: Terminal. The flow ends here; Brief is outside the boundary and this table neither names nor guarantees a Brief launch.

counted_baseline.why_this_block_exists: Acceptance item 2 of kogaki#625 counts waits and writes per run against the table. Stating the baseline figures here makes that count checkable against a declaration rather than against a reading of the array.

non_flow_entry_points.self-test: seam-free identity-cite fixture pass; emits no owner surface, carries no sequencing authority
non_flow_entry_points.validate: runs survey-record validation; emits no owner surface

removed_entry_points.adopt: becomes part of J1_claims' gate re-offer path
removed_entry_points.neighborhood: already retired (kogaki#472/#473); the section rides the Full Report

reader_notes: The table is authoritative over sequencing and over nothing else. A reader looking for what a claim may SAY is in the wrong file (§7); for what a rendered line may LOOK LIKE, report-format.json.

Conformance to this table is mechanically checkable. Whether the declared order is the RIGHT order, whether a wait belongs where it sits, and whether a judgment point is placed where judgment is owed are judgments and route to the review lane (§15.8).

TAG_SELECTION and ID_SELECTION render no gate declaration and must not: they are the owner speaking, and §6.3's question allowlist for that window is empty. A future table row giving either of them a gate would be refused at ratification, not caught at runtime.
The run record holds control state only. It references the survey record by path and holds no ID->slug map, because §14.3 rules the survey record is that map and a second carrier is refused (§15.3).

`renders_gate_declaration` is present and explicit on EVERY state, including the ten that never gate (PR #626 round 1, finding 3). It was carried by absence in v1, which made §15.4's load-bearing claim — that the states between TAG-SELECTION and ID-SELECTION declare no gate, §6.3's one surviving prohibition — indistinguishable from a field somebody forgot. A property the table exists to carry may not be read off a missing key.
removed_entry_points_note: Removed, not flagged debug-only — SPEC §15.7. This discharges §14.1's four uncovered owner surfaces by removing them rather than by grammaring them, taking grammar coverage to two of two.
non_flow_entry_points_note: SPEC §15.7 — stated so their survival reads as a decision rather than an oversight.
